ai.title: Fix toolcall tracking and update Haiku costs
ai.summary: Updated @anthropic-ai/sdk to ^0.33.1 and adjusted Haiku token costs in `backend/src/billing/message-cost-tracker.ts`. Refactored `backend/src/claude.ts` to remove redundant API key checks, switch to `logger.error`, and ensure `saveMessage` runs unconditionally on `message_delta` unless database logging is ignored. Fixed stream processing in `backend/src/process-stream.ts` to continue instead of break on completion. Simplified `start-server` script in root `package.json`.

eli5.text: When you run a server task locally, it no longer tries to connect to a separate database process first, so it starts a bit quicker. Behind the scenes, the cost calculations for a lightweight model were corrected and a bookkeeping counter for tool calls was fixed so internal usage tracking stays accurate. Nothing you see on screen changes right now, but the numbers logged for billing and diagnostics are now correct for Haiku.

ai.title: Rename --pro to --max in CLI and docs
ai.summary: The premium mode flag `--pro` is renamed to `--max`, with `--o1` added as an alias. Internal `costMode` remains 'pro'. Docs in `modes.knowledge.md`, `npm-app/README.md`, and `web/src/content/help/*` reflect the new name and model usage details. CLI help text in `npm-app/src/index.ts` lists `--max, --pro, --o1`.

eli5.text: When you start the coding assistant from a terminal, the special switch for getting better answers is now called --max instead of --pro. If you already type --pro, it still works as a nickname, and you can also use --o1 as another alternative. You'll see the new name --max appear in the built-in help and startup menu, while the instructions and documentation everywhere now say --max and mention which AI models power the higher quality mode.

ai.title: ripgrep prompt clarifies automatic quote handling
ai.summary: System prompt in `backend/src/system-prompt.ts` updated to inform agent that quotes are automatically added around code search patterns. Previous instruction required manual quoting for special characters; now directs user to escape characters like '-' or '.' instead. Affects internal LLM guidance for `code_search` tool.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to search through code for specific patterns, it no longer needs to wrap your search terms in quotation marks manually. The assistant automatically surrounds your search pattern with quotes behind the scenes, so you can type things like import.*foo directly instead of wrapping them. If you want to search for special characters such as hyphens, periods, or backslashes, you'll need to escape them with a backslash instead. This change only affects how the internal system prompt guides the assistant's search behavior, with no visible difference if you don't use special characters.

ai.title: Clarify git push permission in system prompt
ai.summary: Updated system prompt to explicitly state that user requests to commit changes do not imply permission to push. This change modifies the guidelines for the `git commit` and `git rebase` commands in `backend/src/system-prompt.ts`. The update ensures the agent requires explicit permission for push operations, preventing unintended remote repository updates.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to commit changes, it now saves those changes locally without automatically sending them to the shared remote repository. This means you have to explicitly tell it to push the changes if you want them shared with others or stored on GitHub. Previously, the assistant might have pushed without asking. This rule is now in effect for anyone interacting with the assistant.

ai.title: Rename pro mode to max and deprecate --pro flag
ai.summary: Cost mode 'pro' renamed to 'max' across core constants, CLI, and prompts. The --pro flag now triggers a deprecation warning and exits, forcing users to restart with --max. Plan display name changed from 'Pro Max' to 'Pro Plus'. Updates cover backend logic, npm-app CLI, and documentation.

eli5.text: Starting today, the premium subscription you pick from the pricing list now appears as "Pro Plus" instead of "Pro Max" in the plan names. If you use the command-line shortcut that previously selected the top-tier option, that shortcut is no longer accepted and the program will tell you to restart with the new option, then quit. Choosing the higher-cost operating mode makes the assistant answer more complex questions across multiple files; the lower option still keeps answers quick and simple.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.143
ai.summary: Version updated 1.0.142 to 1.0.143. Affects npm-app/package.json. Internal release increment.

eli5.text: The software you use got a small behind-the-scenes update that keeps everything running smoothly, but you probably won't notice anything different on your end. This update fixes how the assistant tracks certain actions, makes the cost estimates more accurate, and includes clearer instructions for the assistant on how to handle specific situations like code commits. These changes were rolled out as part of a regular maintenance release on January 15th, 2025, and are now live for anyone using the tool.

ai.title: Update system prompt for git push and script safety
ai.summary: Tightened command execution guidelines in backend/src/system-prompt.ts to explicitly prohibit `git push` without permission and restrict scripts with side effects. Replaced vague 'probably don't run scripts' with strict side-effect checks, and clarified the 30-second timeout by specifying `npm start` alongside `npm run dev` as examples of forbidden long-running processes.

eli5.text: The assistant received updated guidance on which commands it can run, making it more cautious about actions that could change your code or deploy it remotely. Specifically, the rules now explicitly prohibit pushing code changes to shared repositories unless you directly grant permission, which it previously only implied. If you watched the assistant work, you would notice it asking twice before running any script that makes lasting changes, and you would not see it attempt to upload your code without your clear approval.
